summary: V3 done: the delta suite (verification/delta, 12 cases / 6 fault scenarios for GAP-2 and GAP-17) runs green on the implementation — run_validate(assets=verification/delta) = PASS 12/12 (rie + DynamoDB Local), verdict_delta.json written with an empty failure list, so no triage and no routing. run_coverage(assets=verification/delta) recorded (bestsellers-update 98.9% stmts / 91.5% branches; orders-create 68.2% / 46.2% only because the delta set exercises the success + publish-failure arms — its 400/500/body-parsing arms are exercised by the judge cases). run_equivalence(record, label=B0) recorded 20 runs with infra_errors empty and all 6 scenarios' faults actually firing; the recorded behaviour matches D-6's accepted "claim-then-apply" window and SI-09/SI-10 failure granularity. No tests and no code were changed.
notes: One infra flake worth knowing: the first run_equivalence(record, B0) call died with "DynamoDB Local did not start within 90s (localstack/localstack:3.8)" even though run_validate/run_coverage used the same backend fine; an immediate retry succeeded. Logged as non_blocking V3-INFRA-1, no stage needs to be reworked for it. Advisory observation from the baseline (not a defect, and D-6 already says so explicitly): under add-fails-all the idempotency marker is written before the ADD fails permanently, so a redelivery would skip that element and the increment is lost — that is the "claim then apply" window D-6 chose on purpose; delta-bestsellers-redelivery-after-claim-only asserts exactly it. Coverage numbers are reported only, per the V3 role brief (no threshold). Artifacts: verification/verdict_delta.json (assets_digest 9aee4953f9de4370, code_state = working tree), verification/coverage/{summary,bestsellers-update,orders-create}.json, verification/fault_baseline_B0.json, storage/stage_reports/V3.json. judge/ untouched.
